note: District-level travel guide. Attractions and access details can change; verify locally.

districts.theme: Chalukyan architecture, river landscapes and pilgrimage
districts.overview: Bagalkote is a strong choice for travellers interested in early Deccan temple architecture and the history of the Chalukya period. Its best-known heritage circuit links Badami, Aihole and Pattadakal, which can be explored as a connected multi-day journey. The district also has riverine and religious landscapes around Kudalasangama. Expect substantial walking around archaeological complexes, uneven stone surfaces and exposed sunny areas.

destinations.name: Badami Cave Temples
destinations.detail: Rock-cut cave shrines carved into sandstone cliffs, known for sculptural panels and views across Agastya Lake.

destinations.name: Aihole
destinations.detail: An extensive early temple-town landscape with varied experiments in temple forms and stone architecture.

destinations.name: Pattadakal
destinations.detail: A UNESCO-listed group of Chalukyan monuments showing a notable blend of northern and southern temple styles.

destinations.name: Kudalasangama
destinations.detail: A major spiritual site associated with Basavanna, located near the meeting of rivers.

districts.best_for: History, architecture, photography and pilgrimage
districts.planning: Base the first day around Badami and its cave-temple area. Use the next day for Aihole and Pattadakal, allowing time to explore rather than rushing between monuments. Add Kudalasangama if you have another half-day or day and confirm road conditions and local access. Carry water, sun protection and comfortable footwear.

districts.theme: Fort heritage, mining history and dryland landscapes
districts.overview: Ballari sits in Karnataka's eastern Deccan landscape and is known for its hilltop fort, historic settlements and links to the region's industrial and mining history. The rocky terrain and open viewpoints make it more suitable for heritage walks and short explorations than a packed indoor sightseeing schedule. It can be paired with nearby Vijayanagara district for a wider north-eastern Karnataka heritage trip.

destinations.name: Ballari Fort
destinations.detail: A hill fort spread across rocky elevations, with defensive remains and broad views over the city and surrounding plains.

destinations.name: Sanganakallu
destinations.detail: A prehistoric archaeological landscape associated with early human settlement and stone-tool traditions; visit only where access is permitted.

destinations.name: Toranagallu area
destinations.detail: A useful regional base for travellers combining Ballari with the Hampi–Hospet heritage circuit; the industrial landscape is part of the area's modern history.

districts.best_for: Fort walks, archaeology and regional history
districts.planning: Reserve a cooler morning for Ballari Fort and avoid exposed climbs during the hottest part of the day. Keep a separate half-day for Sanganakallu only after confirming visitor access. If combining with Hampi, plan the transfer as a separate leg and stay near the destination rather than attempting every site in one day.

districts.theme: Forts, temples, waterfalls and Western Ghats edges
districts.overview: Belagavi district offers a varied mix of Maratha-era and regional fort history, religious sites, forested landscapes and seasonal waterfalls. The city of Belagavi works as a practical base for local heritage, while longer excursions require road time. The district is large, so select one cluster of attractions instead of trying to cover distant places in a single day.

destinations.name: Belagavi Fort and Kamal Basadi
destinations.detail: The fort area preserves layers of regional history; Kamal Basadi is noted for its Jain architecture and carved details.

destinations.name: Kittur Fort and Palace
destinations.detail: A heritage site associated with Rani Chennamma and the Kittur resistance history.

destinations.name: Gokak Falls
destinations.detail: A broad waterfall on the Ghataprabha River, most dramatic during and after the monsoon; access and safety depend on water conditions.

destinations.name: Saundatti Yellamma Temple
destinations.detail: A major pilgrimage centre that draws visitors throughout the year, with especially busy festival periods.

districts.best_for: History, pilgrimage, waterfalls and road trips
districts.planning: Spend one day in Belagavi city and its fort area. Use another day for Kittur or Saundatti depending on interests. Treat Gokak Falls as a seasonal excursion and check local warnings during high flow; do not approach unsafe edges.

districts.theme: Fort heritage, countryside temples and short escapes
districts.overview: Bengaluru Rural surrounds the capital with a countryside mix of forts, old temples, village landscapes and short road-trip destinations. It is suitable for half-day or one-day outings from Bengaluru, but public transport and last-mile connections can be limited at smaller sites. Devanahalli is a convenient heritage stop near the airport corridor.

destinations.name: Devanahalli Fort
destinations.detail: A historic fort associated with the birthplace region of Tipu Sultan, with surviving gateways and fort walls.

destinations.name: Ghati Subramanya Temple
destinations.detail: A well-known pilgrimage centre near Doddaballapura, visited for its distinctive temple traditions.

destinations.name: Doddaballapura countryside
destinations.detail: A rural area with traditional settlements, weaving connections and temple stops that work best with a planned local route.

destinations.name: Nelamangala and surrounding heritage villages
destinations.detail: A practical countryside circuit for travellers interested in local temples and rural Karnataka landscapes; identify specific sites before departure.

districts.best_for: Short drives, temples and countryside experiences
districts.planning: Choose Devanahalli Fort with one nearby stop for a half-day outing. For Ghati Subramanya and Doddaballapura, start early and arrange return transport in advance. Check temple schedules and local access before setting out.

districts.theme: Rocky hills, silk craft, forts and nature escapes
districts.overview: Bengaluru South is the current district name for the erstwhile Ramanagara district; Ramanagara remains the district headquarters and a key destination. The district is known for granite hill formations, silk-related craft traditions, reservoirs and historic towns. Rock-climbing and trekking should be undertaken only at permitted locations with suitable guidance and weather conditions.

destinations.name: Ramanagara hills
destinations.detail: Granite hill formations made famous in popular cinema and known for outdoor climbing landscapes; follow access and wildlife-safety rules.

destinations.name: Channapatna
destinations.detail: A craft town famous for lacquered wooden toys and traditional artisan work; a good stop for responsible craft shopping.

destinations.name: Kanakapura countryside
destinations.detail: A base for river, reservoir and nature-oriented outings; water activities must follow operator and local safety guidance.

destinations.name: Magadi and Savandurga region
destinations.detail: A heritage-and-hill circuit with temples and a prominent monolithic hill landscape; trekking requires preparation and current access checks.

districts.best_for: Rock landscapes, craft, short treks and weekend trips
districts.planning: For a one-day outing, combine Ramanagara hills with Channapatna craft visits. For a separate day, explore Magadi and the Savandurga region. Avoid combining distant Kanakapura stops with a rushed hill trek. Confirm that trekking routes are open and use authorised local operators.

districts.theme: City gardens, museums, architecture, food and culture
districts.overview: Bengaluru Urban is Karnataka's capital district and offers a dense city itinerary rather than a single compact monument circuit. Visitors can combine public gardens, museums, historic neighbourhoods, markets, temples and contemporary food districts. Traffic can make short distances take longer than expected, so group places by neighbourhood and use metro or other public transport where practical.

destinations.name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
destinations.detail: A historic botanical garden with mature trees, landscaped spaces and the Glass House; allow time for a relaxed walk.

destinations.name: Cubbon Park and State Central Library area
destinations.detail: A central green space surrounded by civic and heritage architecture.

destinations.name: Bengaluru Palace
destinations.detail: A palace complex reflecting the city's royal-era history; check current visitor arrangements.

destinations.name: Vidhana Soudha and Attara Kacheri
destinations.detail: Iconic civic buildings best appreciated from permitted public viewpoints; security restrictions apply.

destinations.name: National Gallery of Modern Art and museums
destinations.detail: Cultural stops for visitors who want art, science and city history; check weekly closures and ticket information.

districts.best_for: City breaks, gardens, museums, shopping and food
districts.planning: Day 1: Lalbagh, central Bengaluru and nearby museums. Day 2: Palace area, parks and selected neighbourhood food stops. Day 3: choose a theme such as markets, temples or contemporary art. Build the schedule around traffic and opening days; do not assume every attraction is open every day.

districts.theme: Bahmani and Barid Shahi heritage, forts and religious sites
districts.overview: Bidar is one of Karnataka's most distinctive heritage destinations, with a fortified historic core, Islamic-era monuments, traditional metal craft and religious sites. The red laterite plateau gives the area a recognisable landscape. Many monuments are spread across the town and outskirts, so a full day is more comfortable than a quick stopover.

destinations.name: Bidar Fort
destinations.detail: A large fortified complex with gateways, defensive works, palaces and historic structures from the Deccan sultanate period.

destinations.name: Mahmud Gawan Madrasa
destinations.detail: A celebrated educational monument known for its glazed tile decoration and Indo-Persian architectural character.

destinations.name: Bahmani tombs at Ashtur
destinations.detail: A group of royal tombs that help explain Bidar's role in Deccan political history.

destinations.name: Nanak Jhira Sahib
destinations.detail: A prominent Sikh pilgrimage site visited by devotees from different regions.

destinations.name: Bidriware craft workshops
destinations.detail: Traditional metal inlay craft associated with Bidar; buy directly from recognised artisans where possible.

districts.best_for: Architecture, history, crafts and pilgrimage
districts.planning: Spend the first day on Bidar Fort, the madrasa and nearby heritage sites. Add Ashtur and Nanak Jhira on a second day or a carefully planned extended day. Leave time for craft demonstrations and verify monument access locally.

districts.theme: Wildlife, forest landscapes and sacred hills
districts.overview: Chamarajanagar is a gateway to southern Karnataka's forested landscapes and hill shrines. It includes protected habitats and ecologically sensitive areas, so wildlife experiences must follow forest-department rules and authorised safari arrangements. It is best planned as a nature-focused trip with realistic driving times and respect for forest boundaries.

destinations.name: Bandipur National Park
destinations.detail: A major wildlife reserve known for dry and moist deciduous forest habitats and regulated safari experiences.

destinations.name: Biligiri Rangana Hills (BRT Tiger Reserve), Yelandur region
destinations.detail: A biodiverse hill-and-forest landscape with tribal and ecological significance; access is controlled in protected areas.

destinations.name: Male Mahadeshwara Hills
destinations.detail: A forested pilgrimage destination with a hilltop temple and winding approach roads.

destinations.name: Himavad Gopalaswamy Betta
destinations.detail: A hilltop temple and misty landscape within a sensitive forest setting; access may be regulated by authorities.

districts.best_for: Wildlife, forests, hill scenery and pilgrimage
districts.planning: Choose one forest base such as Bandipur or BRT rather than trying to cross multiple reserves in one day. Book safaris only through authorised channels. Keep noise low, never feed wildlife and follow vehicle, photography and timing rules. Check seasonal road and access restrictions.

districts.theme: Hill viewpoints, forts, vineyards and pilgrimage
districts.overview: Chikkaballapura is a popular short-break district north of Bengaluru, with hill viewpoints, rocky terrain, temples and educational heritage. Nandi Hills is the best-known stop, but the wider district has other hill and fort destinations. Sunrise viewpoints can become crowded, and access rules or vehicle restrictions may change, so verify before departure.

destinations.name: Nandi Hills
destinations.detail: A hilltop destination known for sunrise views, fort remains and broad views across the surrounding plains.

destinations.name: Skandagiri (Kalavara Durga)
destinations.detail: A trekking hill near the Nandi region; night or sunrise treks should be done only with required permits and authorised arrangements.

destinations.name: Gudibande Fort
destinations.detail: A hill fort with stepped routes and panoramic views; the climb requires water, footwear and care.

destinations.name: Muddenahalli
destinations.detail: Associated with engineer Sir M. Visvesvaraya and a museum/memorial experience.

destinations.name: Bhoga Nandeeshwara Temple
destinations.detail: An important temple complex at the foothills of Nandi, valued for its historic architecture.

districts.best_for: Sunrise trips, trekking, temples and short escapes
districts.planning: A balanced day trip combines Bhoga Nandeeshwara Temple and Nandi Hills, with an early start. Keep Skandagiri or Gudibande as a separate trek day. Check online booking, parking, trek permits and weather restrictions before travelling.

districts.theme: Coffee country, Western Ghats peaks, waterfalls and forests
districts.overview: Chikkamagaluru is a Western Ghats destination associated with coffee plantations, mountain viewpoints, forest reserves and trekking. Distances between attractions can be significant and monsoon conditions can affect trails and roads. Choose a base such as Chikkamagaluru town, Mudigere or a plantation stay according to the route rather than attempting every attraction from one point.

destinations.name: Mullayanagiri
destinations.detail: A prominent peak with panoramic mountain views; the final approach includes steps and exposed sections.

destinations.name: Baba Budangiri
destinations.detail: A mountain range and pilgrimage landscape associated with local religious traditions and scenic drives.

destinations.name: Hebbe Falls
destinations.detail: A forest-side waterfall experience that may require an authorised local vehicle or access arrangement; verify current rules.

destinations.name: Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary
destinations.detail: A protected forest and reservoir landscape with regulated wildlife activities.

destinations.name: Kudremukh region
destinations.detail: A high-rainfall Western Ghats landscape known for grasslands and trekking subject to permits and forest regulations.

districts.best_for: Mountain scenery, coffee estates, trekking and nature
districts.planning: Day 1: arrive and explore town or a coffee estate. Day 2: Mullayanagiri and Baba Budangiri as a grouped mountain circuit. Day 3: choose a waterfall or forest experience based on current access. Add a separate day for Kudremukh or Bhadra rather than squeezing it into the same route. Monsoon travellers should check trail closures and landslide advisories.

districts.theme: Massive hill fort, wind energy landscapes and ancient sites
districts.overview: Chitradurga is best known for its impressive hill fort, a large defensive complex of walls, gateways, water structures and rocky hill formations. The district is a convenient heritage stop on routes connecting central and northern Karnataka. The fort involves extensive walking and climbing, so allow several hours and avoid the hottest part of the day.

destinations.name: Chitradurga Fort
destinations.detail: A multi-layered hill fort associated with the Nayakas and later regional powers, famous for its gates, ramparts and dramatic boulder landscape.

destinations.name: Chandravalli
destinations.detail: An archaeological and natural site near Chitradurga with cave and settlement associations; confirm visitor access.

destinations.name: Vani Vilas Sagar (Marikanive) Dam
destinations.detail: A historic reservoir and scenic landscape in the district; observe local safety restrictions near water and dam structures.

destinations.name: Hiriyur
destinations.detail: A useful town stop on the Bengaluru–north Karnataka corridor, with nearby regional temples and local food.

districts.best_for: Fort exploration, history, photography and road trips
districts.planning: Give Chitradurga Fort a full morning or afternoon rather than treating it as a 30-minute stop. Add Chandravalli or Vani Vilas Sagar if access and travel time allow. Carry water and wear shoes suitable for uneven rock steps.

districts.theme: Coastal temples, beaches, ports, cuisine and Yakshagana
districts.overview: Dakshina Kannada combines the coastal city of Mangaluru with temple towns, beaches, rivers and a strong food and performing-arts culture. It is a good district for combining pilgrimage, coastal scenery and regional cuisine. The monsoon can bring rough seas and heavy rainfall; beaches and water activities must be approached according to local warnings.

destinations.name: Mangaluru city
destinations.detail: A coastal urban base known for temples, churches, markets, port history and distinctive coastal cuisine.

destinations.name: Dharmasthala
destinations.detail: A major pilgrimage centre in the Western Ghats foothills, known for its temple and community traditions.

destinations.name: Kukke Subrahmanya
destinations.detail: A major pilgrimage destination set amid forested hills; busy festival dates require advance planning.

destinations.name: Panambur and Tannirbhavi beaches
destinations.detail: Popular coastal spaces near Mangaluru; follow lifeguard advice and avoid swimming in rough seas.

destinations.name: Kateel
destinations.detail: A temple destination on the Nandini River, often visited as part of a coastal temple circuit.

districts.best_for: Pilgrimage, beaches, coastal food and culture
districts.planning: Day 1: Mangaluru city and nearby beach, subject to sea conditions. Day 2: choose Dharmasthala or Kukke Subrahmanya; they are separate excursions and should not be rushed together. Add Kateel if route and time permit. Check temple queues, festival traffic and beach advisories.

districts.theme: Local food, reservoirs, temples and central Karnataka heritage
districts.overview: Davanagere is a central Karnataka district that works well as a stop on longer journeys between Bengaluru and northern Karnataka. The city is widely associated with its distinctive benne dosa, while the wider district includes historic temples, tanks and rural heritage. It is more suited to a relaxed food-and-heritage stop than a long resort-style holiday.

destinations.name: Davanagere city food trail
destinations.detail: Try the local benne dosa tradition at established eateries; recipes and spice levels vary by restaurant.

destinations.name: Santhebennur Pushkarani
destinations.detail: A historic stepped tank known for its stone architecture and peaceful setting.

destinations.name: Bagali Kalleshwara Temple
destinations.detail: A historic temple site with architectural and inscriptional interest.

destinations.name: Shanti Sagara (Sulekere), Channagiri
destinations.detail: A large historic lake and water landscape; visit respectfully and follow local access rules.

districts.best_for: Food, temple architecture and a relaxed road stop
districts.planning: Use the city as a food stop and add Santhebennur or Bagali as a half-day heritage excursion. If visiting Shanti Sagara, confirm access and avoid unsafe water edges. Combine with Chitradurga or Shivamogga only if you have enough road time.

districts.theme: Music, education, temples and regional culture
districts.overview: Dharwad is a cultural and educational centre in north Karnataka, strongly associated with Hindustani classical music, literature and regional food. The twin-city area with Hubballi offers a city-based itinerary with historic institutions, temples and markets. It can also serve as a base for nearby heritage sites in Gadag and other northern districts.

destinations.name: Dharwad city heritage and cultural institutions
destinations.detail: Explore the city's literary and music traditions, historic neighbourhoods and institutions; local cultural calendars vary.

destinations.name: Chandramouleshwara Temple, Unkal (Hubballi area)
destinations.detail: A historic temple noted for its architecture and inscriptions, useful as part of a twin-city visit.

destinations.name: Nrupatunga Betta
destinations.detail: A hill viewpoint and urban green space near Hubballi, popular for city views.

destinations.name: Siddharoodha Math
destinations.detail: A prominent spiritual site in Hubballi visited by devotees.

districts.best_for: Music, culture, temples and urban exploration
districts.planning: Spend a day across Dharwad and Hubballi, grouping stops by city to reduce transfers. Ask locally about concerts or cultural programmes rather than assuming performances occur daily. Use Dharwad as a base for a separate day trip to Lakkundi or Gadag if interested in temple architecture.

districts.theme: Chalukyan temples, stepwells and historic towns
districts.overview: Gadag district is an important destination for travellers interested in medieval Deccan temple architecture. Lakkundi is especially valuable for its temples, inscriptions and stepwells, while Dambal and the Gadag town temples add depth to a heritage circuit. These sites are best explored slowly with attention to architectural details.

destinations.name: Lakkundi
destinations.detail: A heritage village with numerous temples, ornate stepwells and important examples of Western Chalukyan architecture.

destinations.name: Trikuteshwara Temple, Gadag
destinations.detail: A major temple complex with carved pillars and architectural features from the Chalukyan period.

destinations.name: Doddabasappa Temple, Dambal
destinations.detail: A notable temple associated with the distinctive stellate plan and detailed stonework.

destinations.name: Kappatagudda
destinations.detail: A hill and biodiversity landscape near Gadag; outdoor visits should follow local conservation and access guidance.

districts.best_for: Temple architecture, archaeology and heritage photography
districts.planning: Day 1: Gadag town and Lakkundi, allowing time for stepwells and smaller temples. Day 2: Dambal and Kappatagudda if access and weather are suitable. Arrange local transport for village sites and avoid climbing on protected structures.

districts.theme: Hoysala architecture, Jain heritage and Western Ghats gateways
districts.overview: Hassan is one of Karnataka's richest districts for temple architecture and heritage travel. Belur and Halebidu are celebrated for their Hoysala sculptural programmes, while Shravanabelagola is a major Jain pilgrimage centre. Sakleshpur offers a different experience with coffee estates and Western Ghats scenery. These attractions lie in different parts of the district, so plan by corridor.

destinations.name: Belur Chennakeshava Temple
destinations.detail: A Hoysala temple known for detailed soapstone sculpture, narrative friezes and richly carved pillars.

destinations.name: Halebidu Hoysaleswara Temple
destinations.detail: A major Hoysala monument with elaborate exterior sculpture and a long, detailed viewing route.

destinations.name: Shravanabelagola
destinations.detail: A major Jain pilgrimage town dominated by the monolithic Gommateshwara statue on Vindhyagiri Hill; the climb involves many steps.

destinations.name: Sakleshpur
destinations.detail: A hill and coffee-growing region with scenic drives, estate stays and outdoor experiences subject to weather and access.

districts.best_for: Hoysala heritage, Jain pilgrimage, coffee hills and architecture
districts.planning: Day 1: Belur and Halebidu as a paired heritage circuit. Day 2: Shravanabelagola, allowing time for the hill climb. Add a separate day for Sakleshpur rather than combining it with all three heritage sites. Check monument and hill access details before travel.

districts.theme: Temple towns, rural heritage and quiet countryside
districts.overview: Haveri district offers a quieter heritage route through north Karnataka, with historic temples, traditional settlements and agricultural landscapes. It is a useful district for travellers who want to explore lesser-known architectural sites between major destinations. Some monuments are in smaller towns and villages, so local transport and advance route planning are helpful.

destinations.name: Bankapura Peacock Sanctuary
destinations.detail: A protected habitat associated with peafowl and dryland ecology; follow forest and sanctuary visitor rules.

destinations.name: Choudayyadanapura Mukteshwara Temple
destinations.detail: A historic temple on the Varada River, valued for its architecture and peaceful rural setting.

destinations.name: Ranebennur Blackbuck Sanctuary
destinations.detail: A grassland habitat known for blackbuck; wildlife sightings are not guaranteed and visits follow sanctuary rules.

destinations.name: Haveri Siddhesvara Temple
destinations.detail: A historic temple in the district headquarters area, useful for a town heritage stop.

districts.best_for: Rural heritage, temples and wildlife landscapes
districts.planning: Use Haveri town as a base for nearby temple visits. Treat Ranebennur and Bankapura as separate nature stops and check seasonal access, entry rules and guidance. Avoid disturbing wildlife or leaving marked routes.

districts.theme: Sufi heritage, Bahmani architecture and Buddhist archaeology
districts.overview: Kalaburagi, formerly known as Gulbarga, is a major heritage centre in the Kalyana Karnataka region. Its monuments reflect the Bahmani and Deccan sultanate periods, while Sannati adds an important Buddhist archaeological dimension. The district is well suited to a history-focused itinerary, with local food and markets adding a city experience.

destinations.name: Gulbarga Fort and Jama Masjid
destinations.detail: A fortified historic complex with a distinctive mosque and major examples of Deccan Islamic architecture.

destinations.name: Khwaja Bande Nawaz Dargah
destinations.detail: A significant Sufi shrine and centre of religious and cultural life.

destinations.name: Sannati and Kanaganahalli
destinations.detail: An important Buddhist archaeological area associated with stupas, inscriptions and ancient remains; access may be controlled.

destinations.name: Malkhed
destinations.detail: A historic settlement associated with the Rashtrakuta period and regional history.

districts.best_for: Deccan history, Sufi heritage and archaeology
districts.planning: Day 1: Kalaburagi Fort, Jama Masjid and the dargah, observing local customs and prayer schedules. Day 2: plan Sannati or Malkhed as a longer excursion with transport arranged in advance. Confirm archaeological access and photography rules.

districts.theme: Coffee estates, forested hills, rivers and Kodava culture
districts.overview: Kodagu (Coorg) is a Western Ghats district known for coffee-growing landscapes, forested hills, river origins and Kodava culture. Madikeri is a common base, while Virajpet, Kushalnagar and other towns suit different routes. Heavy monsoon rain can affect roads, waterfalls and trails, so itinerary flexibility is important.

destinations.name: Madikeri Fort and Raja's Seat
destinations.detail: Town landmarks that introduce Kodagu's history and offer views over the surrounding hills.

destinations.name: Talacauvery and Bhagamandala
destinations.detail: A pilgrimage and landscape circuit associated with the origin of the River Cauvery and the Brahmagiri hills.

destinations.name: Dubare Elephant Camp area
destinations.detail: A river-side tourism area where activities and animal interactions are subject to current operator and animal-welfare rules; verify what is offered.

destinations.name: Nagarhole National Park / Kabini edge
destinations.detail: A protected forest and wildlife landscape; safari access is regulated and must be booked through authorised channels.

destinations.name: Coffee estate experiences
destinations.detail: Plantation walks and tastings can explain coffee cultivation and local life; book with the estate and respect private property.

districts.best_for: Nature, coffee, slow travel, wildlife and culture
districts.planning: Day 1: Madikeri town and viewpoints. Day 2: Talacauvery and Bhagamandala. Day 3: choose a coffee-estate experience or a regulated wildlife activity. Add a day for the Kushalnagar side if visiting the Tibetan settlement and nearby attractions. Avoid overloading the itinerary during monsoon.

districts.theme: Ancient temples, gold-mining history and rocky hills
districts.overview: Kolar district combines ancient temple towns with the industrial heritage of the Kolar Gold Fields. It is a practical short road trip from Bengaluru for visitors interested in architecture, pilgrimage and social history. Some KGF-era structures are industrial or restricted property, so visitors should not enter abandoned or private mine areas without permission.

destinations.name: Kolaramma Temple
destinations.detail: A historic temple in Kolar town known for its traditional architecture and local religious importance.

destinations.name: Someshwara Temple, Kolar
destinations.detail: A notable temple with Vijayanagara-period architectural elements and carved details.

destinations.name: Avani
destinations.detail: A temple and hill landscape associated with the Ramayana tradition and historic shrines.

destinations.name: Kolar Gold Fields (KGF) heritage
destinations.detail: A mining town with a significant colonial-era and industrial history; visit public areas and authorised heritage locations only.

destinations.name: Antargange
destinations.detail: A rocky hill and cave-temple landscape popular for trekking; use permitted routes and suitable guidance.

districts.best_for: Temple heritage, industrial history and trekking
districts.planning: Day 1: Kolar temples and Avani. Day 2: Antargange or a guided, permitted KGF heritage visit. Start hill walks early and do not enter mine shafts, abandoned buildings or restricted industrial property.

districts.theme: Vijayanagara-era heritage, temples and river landscapes
districts.overview: Koppal district contains important heritage sites connected with the wider Vijayanagara region, along with distinctive temple architecture and pilgrimage centres. Anegundi lies across the Tungabhadra from the Hampi landscape and offers a different perspective on the region's historic and mythic geography. It is best combined with Vijayanagara district as a multi-day trip.

destinations.name: Anegundi
destinations.detail: A historic settlement associated with the Kishkindha landscape, traditional homes and access to the Tungabhadra river region.

destinations.name: Mahadeva Temple, Itagi
destinations.detail: A celebrated Kalyana Chalukya temple known for refined stone architecture and ornamentation.

destinations.name: Kanakagiri
destinations.detail: A historic Jain and temple town with a hilltop setting and regional heritage.

destinations.name: Munirabad and Tungabhadra Dam area
destinations.detail: A regional base and reservoir landscape; access to dam facilities is controlled and viewing areas can change.

districts.best_for: Temple architecture, heritage villages and Hampi-region exploration
districts.planning: Pair Anegundi with the Hampi circuit but allow a separate day or half-day for river crossings and village exploration. Visit Itagi as a separate road excursion. Check local boat operations, river levels and monument access; never assume coracle services operate in all conditions.

districts.theme: River heritage, temple towns, birdlife and waterfalls
districts.overview: Mandya is a Cauvery-basin district with a strong agricultural identity and several major heritage and nature attractions. Srirangapatna, Melukote, Ranganathittu and Shivanasamudra each offer a different experience. The district works well for short trips from Mysuru or Bengaluru, but attractions should be grouped geographically to avoid unnecessary backtracking.

destinations.name: Srirangapatna
destinations.detail: An island town on the Cauvery with monuments associated with Tipu Sultan, the Ranganathaswamy Temple and colonial-era history.

destinations.name: Melukote
destinations.detail: A hilltop pilgrimage town known for Cheluvanarayana Swamy Temple, the Yoga-Narasimha shrine and traditional food.

destinations.name: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary
destinations.detail: A river-island bird sanctuary known for boat-based wildlife viewing under regulated conditions.

destinations.name: Shivanasamudra Falls
destinations.detail: A major waterfall system on the Cauvery; viewpoints and access depend on season, water flow and local safety rules.

destinations.name: Kokkarebellur
destinations.detail: A village known for community-associated nesting of birds such as painted storks and pelicans; observe from a respectful distance.

districts.best_for: Heritage, pilgrimage, birding and river scenery
districts.planning: Day 1: Srirangapatna and Ranganathittu, checking sanctuary boat timings. Day 2: Melukote and nearby heritage. Keep Shivanasamudra as a separate excursion, especially during high-flow periods. Birding is seasonal and should be quiet and non-intrusive.

districts.theme: Royal heritage, temples, wildlife and cultural experiences
districts.overview: Mysuru district is a strong all-round destination with royal architecture, museums, gardens, pilgrimage towns and forest-edge experiences. Mysuru city is a practical base, while Nanjangud, Somanathapura, Talakadu, Bylakuppe and the Kabini region require separate excursions. During Dasara and holiday periods, accommodation and roads can be busy.

destinations.name: Mysuru Palace
destinations.detail: The city's best-known royal landmark, with Indo-Saracenic architecture and richly decorated interiors; check current visitor timings and photography rules.

destinations.name: Chamundi Hills
destinations.detail: A hilltop temple and viewpoint overlooking Mysuru; road access and crowd levels vary on festival days.

destinations.name: Mysuru Zoo and Karanji Lake
destinations.detail: Urban nature attractions suitable for a slower family itinerary; check weekly closures and visitor rules.

destinations.name: Somanathapura Chennakeshava Temple
destinations.detail: A Hoysala temple celebrated for detailed sculpture and architectural planning.

destinations.name: Nanjangud and Talakadu
destinations.detail: Nanjangud is a major temple town; Talakadu is known for sand-covered temple remains near the Cauvery.

destinations.name: Bylakuppe
destinations.detail: A Tibetan settlement area known for monasteries and cultural experiences; visitors should respect monastery etiquette.

districts.best_for: Family trips, heritage, culture, temples and wildlife
districts.planning: Day 1: Palace, city heritage and local food. Day 2: Chamundi Hills, Zoo or Karanji Lake. Day 3: choose Somanathapura and Talakadu or Nanjangud. Add a separate day for Bylakuppe or Kabini because of travel distance. During Dasara, plan transport and accommodation early.

districts.theme: Deccan forts, medieval sites and thermal landscape
districts.overview: Raichur is a historic Deccan district positioned between major river systems and known for its fort, medieval temples and archaeological sites. It suits travellers interested in the layered history of the Deccan plateau. Summers can be very hot, so outdoor exploration should be scheduled early and hydration is essential.

destinations.name: Raichur Fort
destinations.detail: A historic fort with layers of Deccan-era construction and views over the town.

destinations.name: Mudgal Fort
destinations.detail: A fortified historic town with gateways and remains that reflect the region's strategic past.

destinations.name: Hatti Gold Mines
destinations.detail: An important mining settlement with industrial and labour history; access to operational areas is restricted.

destinations.name: Maski
destinations.detail: An archaeological site known for an Ashokan inscription and early historic significance; confirm access and interpretation facilities.

districts.best_for: Deccan history, forts and archaeology
districts.planning: Explore Raichur Fort in the morning and plan Mudgal or Maski as a separate road trip. Treat Hatti as an industrial heritage area and visit only public or authorised locations. Avoid exposed outdoor sightseeing in peak afternoon heat.

districts.theme: Waterfalls, Western Ghats forests, dams and heritage
districts.overview: Shivamogga district is a gateway to the central Western Ghats, with waterfalls, forest landscapes, reservoirs and historic sites. Jog Falls is the best-known attraction, while Agumbe, Kodachadri, Keladi and Ikkeri offer different nature and heritage experiences. Monsoon scenery can be spectacular, but heavy rain may close roads, trails or viewpoints.

destinations.name: Jog Falls
destinations.detail: A major waterfall on the Sharavathi River; the appearance and safe viewing access change with reservoir releases and season.

destinations.name: Agumbe
destinations.detail: A high-rainfall rainforest region known for sunsets, biodiversity and winding ghat roads.

destinations.name: Kodachadri
destinations.detail: A Western Ghats trekking and pilgrimage destination; routes and vehicle access are subject to forest rules and weather.

destinations.name: Keladi and Ikkeri
destinations.detail: Historic sites associated with the Keladi Nayakas, with notable temple architecture.

destinations.name: Tyavarekoppa Lion and Tiger Safari area
destinations.detail: A regulated wildlife facility near Shivamogga; check current operations and visitor rules.

districts.best_for: Waterfalls, trekking, forests, wildlife and history
districts.planning: Day 1: Shivamogga town and nearby attractions. Day 2: Jog Falls and surrounding viewpoints. Day 3: choose Agumbe or Keladi–Ikkeri. Reserve a separate day for Kodachadri and confirm permits, guide requirements and weather. During monsoon, keep backup plans and avoid flooded roads.

districts.theme: Hill forts, temples, lakes and rural escapes
districts.overview: Tumakuru district offers a mix of hilltop temples, forts, lakes and pilgrimage sites within reach of Bengaluru. Devarayanadurga is a popular hill destination, while Madhugiri Fort provides a more demanding climb. The district's attractions are spread out, so a good itinerary focuses on one or two clusters rather than crossing the district repeatedly.

destinations.name: Devarayanadurga
destinations.detail: A hill landscape with temple sites, forested slopes and viewpoints; road and trekking access depend on local conditions.

destinations.name: Madhugiri Fort
destinations.detail: A large hill fort known for a steep climb and panoramic views; it requires fitness, suitable footwear and safe weather.

destinations.name: Namada Chilume
destinations.detail: A natural spring and forest-side attraction near Devarayanadurga, with local cultural associations.

destinations.name: Siddaganga Math
destinations.detail: A major educational and spiritual institution near Tumakuru; visitors should respect institutional schedules and etiquette.

destinations.name: Goravanahalli Mahalakshmi Temple
destinations.detail: A prominent pilgrimage site in the district.

districts.best_for: Hill walks, temples and day trips
districts.planning: A one-day route can combine Devarayanadurga, Namada Chilume and Siddaganga depending on time. Keep Madhugiri as a separate climb day and start early. Avoid climbing in rain, strong winds or extreme heat; confirm local access.

districts.theme: Temple heritage, beaches, islands and coastal cuisine
districts.overview: Udupi district combines a famous temple town with beaches, estuaries, islands and coastal food traditions. It is well suited to a relaxed coastal holiday, but sea conditions and monsoon weather strongly affect swimming, boating and beach access. The district's attractions stretch along the coast, so plan north–south travel in clusters.

destinations.name: Sri Krishna Matha, Udupi
destinations.detail: A major pilgrimage centre with distinctive temple traditions and a busy surrounding market area.

destinations.name: Malpe Beach and St Mary's Islands
destinations.detail: A coastal recreation area and island group; boat services are weather- and season-dependent and may be suspended.

destinations.name: Kaup Lighthouse and Beach
destinations.detail: A scenic coastal stop with a lighthouse and beach; access to the lighthouse may have separate timings.

destinations.name: Maravanthe Beach
destinations.detail: A distinctive coastal road landscape where the Arabian Sea and Souparnika River run close on opposite sides of the highway.

destinations.name: Kollur Mookambika Temple
destinations.detail: A major pilgrimage destination in the forested Western Ghats region.

districts.best_for: Beach holidays, pilgrimage, food and coastal photography
districts.planning: Day 1: Udupi town, Krishna Matha and local cuisine. Day 2: Malpe, St Mary's Islands if boats operate, and Kaup. Day 3: choose Maravanthe or Kollur as a separate excursion. Avoid swimming during rough-sea warnings and verify boat operations before travelling.

districts.theme: Beaches, forests, rivers, forts and Western Ghats biodiversity
districts.overview: Uttara Kannada is one of Karnataka's most geographically diverse districts, extending from the Western Ghats forests to the Arabian Sea. It includes beach towns, river estuaries, waterfalls, temples and protected forests. Distances are long and roads can be winding; plan a coastal cluster or forest cluster rather than trying to cover the whole district in one visit.

destinations.name: Gokarna
destinations.detail: A coastal pilgrimage town known for Mahabaleshwar Temple and beaches such as Om and Kudle; sea conditions vary.

destinations.name: Murudeshwar
destinations.detail: A coastal pilgrimage destination with a prominent Shiva statue and temple complex.

destinations.name: Dandeli and Kali River region
destinations.detail: A forest-and-river destination known for regulated adventure activities and wildlife experiences; use licensed operators.

destinations.name: Yana rock formations
destinations.detail: Distinctive karst rock formations reached by a forest walk; trail conditions vary, especially in monsoon.

destinations.name: Sathodi Falls and Unchalli Falls
destinations.detail: Waterfall destinations in forested settings; access roads and safe viewing areas are seasonal.

destinations.name: Karwar and Devbagh
destinations.detail: Coastal town and island-side scenery with boating subject to weather and authorised operations.

districts.best_for: Coast, forest, waterfalls, adventure and nature
districts.planning: Choose a northern coast route around Karwar and Gokarna, or a forest route around Dandeli and Yana. Murudeshwar can be paired with a coastal journey. Do not combine Dandeli, Gokarna and Karwar as casual same-day stops. Check forest permissions, waterfall access and sea warnings.

districts.theme: UNESCO heritage landscape, temples, boulder hills and river culture
districts.overview: Vijayanagara district contains the Hampi heritage landscape, one of India's most important archaeological destinations. The region includes temple complexes, royal enclosures, market streets, reservoirs and dramatic granite boulder scenery. Hampi is spread across a wide area, so visitors should plan at least two full days and consider a local guide for historical context.

destinations.name: Hampi Group of Monuments
destinations.detail: A UNESCO World Heritage Site preserving the remains of the Vijayanagara capital, including temples, royal structures and urban infrastructure.

destinations.name: Vittala Temple and Stone Chariot
destinations.detail: A celebrated monument complex known for its stone chariot and ornate architectural features.

destinations.name: Virupaksha Temple and Hampi Bazaar
destinations.detail: A living temple and historic bazaar corridor that anchors the sacred centre of Hampi.

destinations.name: Hemakuta Hill and Matanga Hill viewpoints
destinations.detail: Rocky hill areas offering views over the heritage landscape; use marked routes and take care on exposed rocks.

destinations.name: Daroji Sloth Bear Sanctuary
destinations.detail: A protected habitat near Hampi; wildlife viewing depends on season and official visitor arrangements.

districts.best_for: World heritage, archaeology, photography and cultural travel
districts.planning: Day 1: sacred centre, Virupaksha Temple and nearby monuments. Day 2: royal centre, Vittala Temple and Stone Chariot, allowing time for walking and transfers. Day 3: Anegundi or Daroji if transport and access allow. Carry water, sun protection and respect monument boundaries.

districts.theme: Adil Shahi architecture, domes, mosques and Deccan history
districts.overview: Vijayapura, formerly Bijapur, is a major heritage city associated with the Adil Shahi dynasty. Its monuments include monumental domes, mosques, palaces and water structures that illustrate the region's architectural and engineering history. Many attractions are within the city, making it suitable for a compact two-day walking-and-driving itinerary.

destinations.name: Gol Gumbaz
destinations.detail: The monumental mausoleum of Mohammed Adil Shah, famous for its massive dome and whispering gallery.

destinations.name: Ibrahim Rauza
destinations.detail: A finely proportioned mausoleum and mosque complex noted for ornamental detail and balanced architecture.

destinations.name: Jama Masjid
destinations.detail: A historic congregational mosque and important example of Adil Shahi architecture.

destinations.name: Bara Kaman
destinations.detail: An unfinished mausoleum complex with dramatic arches and a distinctive historical story.

destinations.name: Upli Buruj
destinations.detail: A historic watchtower and cannon position offering views across the city.

districts.best_for: Architecture, photography and Deccan history
districts.planning: Day 1: Gol Gumbaz, Ibrahim Rauza and nearby city monuments. Day 2: Jama Masjid, Bara Kaman and Upli Buruj. Respect active places of worship, check monument access and group stops by location to reduce travel time.

districts.theme: Hill forts, river valleys and lesser-known Deccan heritage
districts.overview: Yadgir is a quieter Kalyana Karnataka destination with hill forts, historic towns and river landscapes. It is suited to travellers interested in offbeat Deccan history rather than heavily developed tourism infrastructure. Plan transport in advance and carry essentials, as facilities may be limited at smaller sites.

destinations.name: Yadgir Fort
destinations.detail: A hilltop fort overlooking the town, with defensive remains and views across the surrounding plateau.

destinations.name: Shorapur (Surpur) and its heritage sites
destinations.detail: A historic principality area associated with local rulers and regional resistance history.

destinations.name: Wagangera Fort
destinations.detail: A historic fort site in the district's broader heritage landscape; access and conservation status should be checked locally.

destinations.name: Sannati region (nearby Kalaburagi district boundary)
destinations.detail: A major Buddhist archaeological area is in neighbouring Kalaburagi district, so verify district boundaries and route before including it.

districts.best_for: Offbeat forts, local history and rural landscapes
districts.planning: Explore Yadgir Fort in the cooler hours and arrange local transport for Shorapur. Confirm access to fort structures and avoid climbing unstable walls. Pair with Kalaburagi only as a multi-day regional route, not as an assumed nearby stop.
